finite_default_domain.scope: Entire default sampler domain. Explicit fixture parameters outside this range are separately checked; no duplicate padding for production.

provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The native rule treats the input as one down-stroke of a zigzag. The output repeats the band by ping-ponging along the stacking axis: the input, then lines h-2..0, then 1..h-1, then h-2..0. That gives a total length of 4(h-1)+1, with the cross-axis size and colours unchanged. The factory works out where the native row axis lands under the D4 map. With d4%4 = 0 it stays vertical, input at the top, growing down. With 1 it becomes horizontal, input at the right edge, growing left. With 2 it is vertical, input at the bottom, growing up. With 3 it is horizontal, input at the left edge, growing right. The d4>=4 row-reversal only flips native columns, so it does not change the stacking axis. The emitted program bounces directly in visible coordinates. When the band is anchored at the start, it appends reflected and forward sweeps after the input. When it is anchored at the end, it prepends the mirrored sweeps: lines n-1..1, then 0..n-2, then n-1..1. This places the input at the far end, matching the visibly transformed outputs. Colours are copied as-is, so the palette needs no constants.
draft_notes.limitations: The axis and anchor are fixed by d4 rather than inferred from the demonstrations. The constructor's domain always has a band thickness of at least 3 along the stacking axis (stretch>=1). For degenerate thickness below 2 the program returns the input unchanged. No constructor defects or fixture contradictions were found: both train pairs and the test pair match the 4(h-1)+1 ping-pong rule.

independent_source_review.mechanism: The input is one zigzag stroke of height h. Its top row has marks at c%4==2, its middle rows at odd c, and its bottom row at c%4==0. The output ping-pongs the band along the stacking axis: rows 0..h-1, then h-2..0, then 1..h-1, then h-2..0. That gives length 4(h-1)+1. Width and colour are copied unchanged. The emitted solver fixes the stacking axis and anchor end from d4%4. When the band is anchored at the start it appends the back, forward and back sweeps. When it is anchored at the end it prepends sweeps n-1..1, then 0..n-2, then n-1..1. All of this happens directly in visible coordinates.
evidence: Constructor: grid height = 2+stretch (h) and output height = 5+4*stretch = 4(h-1)+1. With stretch in 1..4, input heights are 3..6 and output heights 9..21, all within 30.
Odd columns: r + k(s+1) for r in 1..s and k in 0..3.

This is exactly the ping-pong with period 2(h-1). The bottom input row lands at s+1 and 3(s+1), the top row at 0, 2(s+1) and 4(s+1). Every non-endpoint output row is a middle row, and all middle input rows are identical, so the reflection is well defined.
Fixtures check by hand: height 4 gives 13 rows, height 3 gives 9 rows, height 5 gives 17 rows. Each matches the archived transform's vstack of g, g[h-2..0], g[1..h-1], g[h-2..0].
Factory, k=2 (180° rotation) checked by hand:
The reversed native sequence g0..g_{h-2}, g_{h-1}..g1, g0..g_{h-2}, g_{h-1}..g0 becomes, in g' indices, n-1..1, 0..n-2, n-1..1, 0..n-1.
This equals the prepend order [back, fwd, back, g].
Reflection d4>=4: the input is left-right symmetric (2↔14, 0↔16, odd↔odd under c→16-c). A column reversal therefore leaves the stacking axis unaffected, consistent with the factory comment.

No hidden latents affect the label. stretch and color are both visible (band height and ink), and the colour is copied rather than mapped, so no palette constants or colour-association evidence are needed.

Orientation evidence: under the vertical-flip D4 variants the top and bottom rows swap their mark phases (2 mod 4 vs 0 mod 4). Demonstrations visibly show the growth direction, so the axis/anchor constants are taught orientation constants and not a whole-grid untransform wrapper.
Host audit passed: 1000 fresh pairs, 8000 augmented checks, 16 fixture variants, and no sampler rejections.
nonblocking_limits: The axis and anchor are fixed by d4 rather than inferred from the demonstrations. This is acceptable because demonstrations always show the growth direction in the same augmented frame.
The constructor domain is narrow: width is always 17, stretch is 1..4, and there is one colour. That gives 36 unique base inputs, matching the audit's unique_base_inputs=36.
The n<2 fallback (return the input unchanged) is outside the constructor domain, which always has h>=3, so it is never exercised.
The solver relies on the generated structure. Middle rows are identical, so other bounce variants would coincide on middle rows, but they diverge at endpoint rows, which the demos pin down.
required_context_checks: Confirm the standard D4 context policy (reject D4 variants with the same visible demonstrations and query but conflicting answers) is applied. Left-right-symmetric inputs make reflected variants visibly identical, but they produce identical outputs, so no conflict is expected.
